summary: CRITICAL BUG in the new 'View full recipe' fix on the import preview. The import-view-full button DOES appear and DOES navigate to /recipe with the loader correctly suppressed (providedContent branch), but the numbered Instructions render as '1. [object Object]  2. [object Object] ... 7. [object Object]' because import.tsx openFullRecipe() maps preview.instructions with `s?.text || s?.step || String(s)` — the backend (convert_to_standard_recipe in routes/import_recipe.py) returns each instruction as {stepNumber, instruction, time, visualCue, technique} where the actual step text lives under the key `instruction`, not `text`/`step`. Same broken mapping is used to build the `steps` param passed to /cook, so Cook hands-free shows 'Step 7 of 7' with body '[object Object]' — cook mode is unusable from an imported recipe. Ingredients render correctly (mapper checks i?.name which matches backend schema {name, amount, category, notes}). Everything else in the review passes: import-view-full button exists next to import-save+import-again; navigation to /recipe works; title/description/Italian/25 minutes/Easy meta rendered; save-detail + cook-mode + close-recipe buttons present; the 'Our chef is writing…' loader is NOT shown on the provided-content path (0 POST /api/recipes/detailed calls when opening via this path — verified by network hook). Photo path could not be exercised on headless web (camera not available) — validated Text path per review agent-to-agent note. Regression for the normal Discover -> recipe-card path was attempted but recipe generation timed out in the browser session before cards rendered; the code path itself in recipe.tsx is correct — POST /api/recipes/detailed is only skipped when providedContent is truthy (useQuery.enabled = !providedContent), so opening a mood-generated recipe (no `content` param) will still fetch as before. Reproducible: register vf_test+<ts>@example.com/Test1234 -> paywall Test valid purchase -> /import -> import-tab-text -> paste Spaghetti Aglio e Olio -> import-submit -> import-view-full -> scroll -> steps show [object Object].

ui_bugs.issue: Numbered Instructions on /recipe (opened via View full recipe) render as '1. [object Object]' for every step. Root cause: line 105 maps preview.instructions with `s?.text || s?.step || String(s)` but the AI-normalised instruction objects use the key `instruction` (see backend routes/import_recipe.py IMPORT_RECIPE_PROMPT lines 67-75 -> {stepNumber, instruction, time, visualCue, technique}). Fallback stringifies to '[object Object]'. Fix: change to `s?.text || s?.step || s?.instruction || String(s)` (or map the richer shape into a friendlier line). Reference: /app/frontend/app/import.tsx:105

Same broken mapping produces `steps=['[object Object]',...]` inside the content markdown, so parseSteps() in recipe.tsx returns literally ['[object Object]', ...] and Cook hands-free shows '[object Object]' on every step -> feature unusable from an imported recipe. Reference: /app/frontend/app/import.tsx:105 (steps mapper), /app/frontend/app/recipe.tsx:14-30 (parseSteps).

integration_issues.flow: Import (text) -> View full recipe -> Cook hands-free
integration_issues.issue: Preview shape from POST /api/mobile-import/text has instructions as objects with key `instruction`; frontend mapper only checks `text`/`step` and falls through to String(obj). No API failure — pure client-side field mapping bug. Ingredients work because backend `name` matches the mapper's `i?.name` check.

action_items: Fix /app/frontend/app/import.tsx line 105 openFullRecipe(): extend the step mapper to also read the AI schema key `instruction`. Suggested one-liner: `const steps = (preview.instructions || []).map((s: any) => (typeof s === 'string' ? s : s?.text || s?.step || s?.instruction || (s?.stepNumber && s?.instruction ? s.instruction : String(s))));`. Consider optionally appending `time`/`visualCue` for richer hands-free prompts.

After the fix, re-run: /import -> import-tab-text -> paste a recipe with numbered steps -> import-submit -> import-view-full -> confirm Instructions render real sentences AND cook-mode /cook shows real step text (not [object Object]).
critical_code_review_comments: import.tsx:104 ingredient mapper correctly handles the backend schema `{name, amount, ...}` via `i?.name`. But step mapper on the very next line missed the analogous `s?.instruction` key -> silent [object Object] regression that only surfaces after tapping import-view-full or cook-mode.

recipe.tsx providedContent path is implemented correctly: useQuery.enabled=!providedContent skips the /api/recipes/detailed call (verified by network hook: 0 calls on the import path) and the loader 'Our chef is writing…' is not shown. The bug is entirely upstream in import.tsx feeding it garbage content.

recipe.tsx parseSteps regex `/^\d+\.\s+/` is fine but it now happily returns ['[object Object]', ...] because those literal strings satisfy the pattern. Not the bug's fault, but a defensive filter (`.filter(s => !s.includes('[object'))`) would prevent this class of crash-later failure.

openFullRecipe passes the entire assembled markdown via router params — the URL query for a long recipe already exceeds 1KB. Fine for now but worth watching for very long AI outputs; consider a lightweight in-memory store or route param compression.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Reproduce path (works headlessly, no camera): register any new email/Test1234 -> /paywall -> paywall-subscribe -> confirm-buy -> click text 'Test valid purchase' in RC overlay -> /import -> import-tab-text -> fill import-text with any recipe containing 'Instructions:' + numbered steps -> import-submit -> wait ~12-30s for AI -> import-view-full appears -> click it -> scroll on /recipe to see the Instructions section. After the fix the numbered lines must contain real step text (e.g. 'Bring a large pot of salted water to boil…') NOT '[object Object]'. Also click cook-mode and confirm the visible step body is real text. Preview ingredients already render correctly today (mapper uses i?.name which matches). The regression path (Discover -> mood -> meal -> dietary -> cuisine -> tap recipe-card) uses the same /recipe screen but with NO `content` param, so useQuery(['detailed-recipe', title]) fires POST /api/recipes/detailed as before — this path is unaffected by the bug and only needs a smoke check.
rca_of_issue: Root cause: /app/frontend/app/import.tsx openFullRecipe() line 105 uses `s?.text || s?.step || String(s)` to unwrap each preview.instructions item, but the backend's convert_to_standard_recipe (routes/import_recipe.py IMPORT_RECIPE_PROMPT) normalises every instruction to `{stepNumber, instruction, time, visualCue, technique}`. Neither `text` nor `step` exists on that object, so JS falls through to `String(s)` which yields the literal string '[object Object]'. That poisoned string is then (a) joined into the markdown passed as ?content to /recipe (renders '1. [object Object]' etc.) and (b) later parsed by recipe.tsx parseSteps() into ['[object Object]', ...] which is passed to /cook. Mitigation: add `|| s?.instruction` (and optionally handle stepNumber-based fallback) to the mapper. One-word/one-token fix. Ingredients path is fine because the backend key `name` matches the mapper's `i?.name`.
